claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 has relatively high porosity.
The porosity and low structural integrity of conventional ZrB2 contribute to failure during long-duration exposure to a liquid plating bath.
Adding approximately 0.5 wt% nanoscale silicon during spark plasma sintering will permit preparation of single-phase ZrB2 at approximately 2000 °C.
The silicon additive acts as a transient liquid-phase sintering aid.
At approximately 2000 °C, nanoscale silicon partially melts and forms a transient silicon-rich liquid phase.
The transient silicon-rich liquid phase promotes rapid rearrangement of ZrB2 particles.
The transient liquid phase causes capillary-driven densification.
Capillary-driven densification fills microstructural voids and minimizes pore formation.
During cooling, silicon diffuses into the ZrB2 matrix or otherwise becomes undetectable.
The silicon-aided process produces a nearly pure ZrB2 phase.
Silicon-aided ZrB2 will be denser and have fewer pores than conventionally high-temperature-sintered ZrB2.
The reduced porosity will improve the mechanical integrity of ZrB2.
The denser microstructure will reduce hole formation during prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
The denser microstructure will reduce structural failure during prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
The proposed processing window is spark plasma sintering at approximately 2000 °C for 30 minutes under high-purity argon with approximately 0.5 wt% nanoscale silicon.

contradictions.description: The stated performance baseline is conventionally sintered ZrB2 prepared above 2300 °C, but the experimental control is undoped ZrB2 spark-plasma-sintered at 2000 °C. Thus, the experiment does not directly test the predicted comparison with the stated conventional baseline.
